 Jamal Murray (shin) and Christian Braun (calf) have been upgraded to probable for Monday’s matchup with the Rockets.
 Denver’s top six players were listed on Sunday’s injury report as questionable before getting this positive upgrade on Monday. The Nuggets’ starting five and Sixth Man DeMar DeRozan are all on track to take the court against Houston in a Western Conference powerhouse showdown.

 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Jamal Murray accounted for 38 points (14-of-23 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and five three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 Well, Murray and Nikola Jokić had productive nights on Monday, but the other Nuggets starters played as if they’d left their skills in Mexico City. Murray shot 9-of-14 from the field in the second half, scoring 23 of his game-high 38 points. Based on his preseason ADP, fantasy managers expected Murray to deliver second-round value. Through nine games, he’s been a first-round player in 12-team formats. 
 Nikola Jokić 
 DEN 
 Center 
 #15 
 Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cameron Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokić will start Monday’s game against the Rockets. 
 All five Nuggets’ starters were upgraded from questionable to probable on Monday afternoon, and they’re now available. The Nuggets will roll out their usual starting five against the Rockets. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray (shin) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets. 
 It’s unclear when the injury happened, but fantasy managers should be on the lookout closer to Monday’s contest. Murray is averaging 24.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 6.1 assists on the season, and has not yet missed a game. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun (calf) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets. 
 The Nuggets return from Mexico City with a crowded injury report, as all six of their top players are questionable for Monday. If Braun can’t play, Spencer Jones could start, though his playing time may not increase much since Saturday’s game was his first of the season. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray recorded 16 points (6-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Nuggets. 
 Murray had a relatively quiet day at the office, scoring seven of his 16 points in the fourth quarter to help seal the victory. Category-league managers will be pleased with the rebounds and assists, but it would have been nice to see Murray end his week with a more prolific scoring performance. The Nuggets play three games in Week 4. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray put up 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, a steal and two 3-pointers in win over Raptors on Wednesday. 
 Jamal Murray didn’t have the most efficient night but still filled up the stat sheet in the win. He really got going in the second half which helped the Nuggets take off in the third quarter. We know who Jamal Murray is, and there’s no need to complain too much. He’ll bounce back and his next opportunity to do so will be against the Pacers on Saturday. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 35 points (10-of-19 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, one block and four three-pointers in a 118-110 loss to the Trail Blazers on Monday. 
 Murray has been on a tear since the season opener. He was held to just six points in that game but has averaged 31.6 points, 6.2 assists, 1.2 steals and 5.4 triples while shooting 52.1 percent from the floor and 52.9 percent from deep in their five games since. This was his third game with at least 35 points in that stretch, and while it wasn’t enough for them to win, he continues to be a fantasy star and will look to stay hot against the Raptors on Wednesday. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun had 31 points (11-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, three steals, and seven 3-pointers in 127-120 win over the Suns. 
 Braun went crazy in the first half and hit most of his shots which led to this stat line. Braun has gotten three steals in the past three games when his career average is 0.7 steals, so expect some regression to happen. If the steals become more of a consistent appearance from Braun, there is room for him to be a useful guy in redraft leagues. 
 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jamal Murray put up a monster performance of 39 points (10-of-18 FGs, 12-of-15 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, seven 3-pointers, and five turnovers in win over the Suns. 
 Jamal Murray was an absolute monster in the third quarter, getting 15 points and was the reason they got secure lead. He got to the line 15 times and hit them at 80% which should be a nice boost to your FT% category. He’s been what you hoped for if you drafted him in the top 20 this season. He won’t shoot this efficiently every night, but barring injury he’ll continue to do what he’s doing. 
 Christian Braun 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Christian Braun accounted for 15 points (6-of-13 FGs), four assists, three steals, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans. 
 Braun’s 15 points matched his season high, and just as important for fantasy managers were the other categories. He didn’t grab any rebounds, but the assists and steals should benefit category-league managers. Braun’s coming off a disappointing 2025-26, and the Nuggets need him to bounce back if they’re to be a true contender in the West.

 Victor Wembanyama finished Monday’s win over the Suns with 40 points (15-of-19 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), 11 rebounds, three assists, eight blocks and two three-pointers.
 Simply put, the Suns looked powerless to slow down Wembanyama, let alone stop him. The Spurs’ center matched his season high with eight blocks, the second time in five days that he’s hit that number. Offensively, he missed just four shots from the field, with 12 of his 15 makes coming in the restricted area. With the Spurs visiting the Bulls on Wednesday, Wemby could be in for another huge night at the office. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Cooper Flagg 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Player Stats

 Cooper Flagg authored a dominant performance to lead the Mavericks to a 125-122 win over the Pacers on Monday, delivering a season-high 43 points (16-of-25 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block over 38 minutes.
 Unreal. Flagg delivered 16 clutch points in the fourth quarter alone, joining veteran teammate Kyrie Irving to account for 78 of Dallas’ 125 points in an impressive victory. The 19-year-old prodigy has now scored at least 20 points in seven of his first 10 games, delivering first-round fantasy value while averaging an elite 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists, 2.2 steals and 0.8 blocks per contest. It’s difficult to imagine a more encouraging start to the season for rising superstar still in his teens.
 -  George Bissell

 Pascal Siakam 
 IND 
 Forward 
 #43 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Pascal Siakam amassed a team-high 29 points (9-of-16 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), nine rebounds, eight assists and two steals over 35 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Mavericks.
 Siakam came within one board and two assists of a triple-double, but it wasn’t enough to overcome a herculean performance by Dallas star Cooper Flagg. He knocked down 5-of-8 from three-point range and fell one-point shy of matching his previous season-high mark that he set during Indiana’s season opener against the Pelicans. The 32-year-old forward has delivered seventh-round fantasy value this season, averaging a robust 22.2 points, 6.8 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.1 blocks through 10 games.
 -  George Bissell

 Kyrie Irving matched a season-high with 35 points (11-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs) and four assists over 38 minutes in Monday’s win over the Pacers.
 It was a two-man show for Dallas in this one with Irving and Cooper Flagg combining for an eye-popping 78 of their 125 points. The pair hoisted 43 shot attempts total and connected on 10-of-16 three-pointers. Seven of those conversions from long range came courtesy of Irving as he put together one of his best shooting efforts in recent memory, matching his previous season-high mark in the scoring department set against the Rockets back on October 30. The 34-year-old point guard is putting together an impressive campaign, averaging 22.9 points, 3.2 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.2 steals through nine games.

 DeMar DeRozan produced seven points (2-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds and two assists in Monday’s loss to the Rockets.
 Unfortunately for those who hoped that DeRozan would remain a valuable fantasy option in Denver, it may be time to move on. The veteran wing played 19 minutes off the bench on Monday, and as has been the case on many occasions, the fit looked awkward on offense. The role he’s been asked to play in Denver is far different from any other stop in his career, and it has drastically affected DeRozan’s fantasy value. He’s rostered in 38 percent of Yahoo leagues, and that number may be too high.

 Player Stats

 Nikola Jokić finished Monday’s loss to the Rockets with 25 points (11-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 16 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer.
 Jokić finished Monday’s defeat with his second straight double-double and seventh of the season. Three-point shooting remains an issue for the Nuggets center, who shot 1-of-5 on Monday and is now making 22.5 percent of his attempts this season. Jokić is a career 36 percent shooter from deep, so it’s fair to assume he’ll turn things around eventually. Plus, he brings too much to the table for fantasy managers to panic over subpar production in one category.

 Jabari Smith Jr. accounted for 14 points (6-of-13 FGs), seven rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
 After a quiet first half, Smith shot 4-of-6 from the field in the second half, scoring 10 points. Since scoring 52 points in the Rockets’ final two games of October, he’s cooled off offensively. However, Smith has reached double figures in all four of Houston’s games this month and continues to outperform his ADP (92) by a safe distance.

 Alperen Şengün finished Monday’s win over the Nuggets with 20 points (9-of-17 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
 Like Kevin Durant, Şengün finished Monday’s victory two assists shy of a triple-double. The Rockets center held his own against three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokić, playing efficient basketball as both a scorer and a playmaker. Şengün is closing in on first-round value in 12-team leagues, a few spots ahead of his preseason ADP (18). While some may consider selling high, they should also consider that this may be who Şengün is at this point in his career and hold onto him.
